results.note: One whole three-lobed leaf in red and green autumn colour, held in front of a hemlock branch; outline and toothed edge are readable. Autumn colour sets growth_stage autumn and usual_look false.
Many backlit autumn leaves hang on twigs, overlapping and tilted, so no single outline or margin reads without close study. Backlight changes the colour; crowding makes alone false.
A ground carpet of fallen red and brown leaves; each leaf is small in the frame and crowded. The subject is fallen, dead leaves, so dead_leaf.

Several autumn-coloured leaves on a sapling, overlapping each other; a few outlines are whole and readable but the teeth need close study. Crowding makes alone false; autumn colour sets usual_look false.
One whole red leaf lying on the forest floor among brown fallen leaves and a mushroom; the outline and edge are clear. It is a fallen, dead leaf, so dead_leaf.
A leafy branch of green summer leaves with red stalks; several whole outlines show but the leaves overlap and the teeth are small in the frame. Crowding makes alone false.
A scene of a sapling with red and yellow autumn leaves among other plants; the leaves blend into a mass and no outline or margin can be read.
Autumn-coloured leaves on a twig with the red stalks joining it in opposite pairs; the top leaf is whole but neighbours crowd it and the teeth need close study. Autumn colour sets usual_look false.
One whole green leaf on a red stalk against a soft background; outline, toothed margin and palmate veins are clear. The stalk's join to the twig is at the frame top, so arrangement needs a search.

Close view of one red and green autumn leaf with clear teeth and veins; the frame edge trims a lobe tip and other leaves surround it, so whole and alone are false. Autumn colour sets usual_look false.

A crowded branch of yellow autumn leaves, overlapping and partly soft, against bright sun and a red tree in the background; no single leaf outline or margin reads without study and the frame cuts leaves off. Strong sun and backlight shift the colour; autumn colour makes usual_look false.
A whole moss-covered trunk seen from a distance; the bark ridges are small in the frame and the moss hides the colour, so texture, pattern and colour need close study.
Base of a multi-stemmed trunk with furrowed, scaly bark readable on the front stems. Backlight from the sun between the stems washes out part of the frame and shifts the colour.
Close frame of grey, scaly, vertically furrowed bark with no trunk edge or scale object, so it shows texture only. The centre is sharp; only the corners soften.
A straight trunk filling the frame with both edges visible, showing grey bark broken into long, narrow, shaggy vertical plates; a clean, typical mature bark view.
A trunk with both edges in frame, smooth grey bark beginning to break into thin, flaking brownish plates; a transitional bark that reads clearly.

The camera looks up the trunk into the crown against a strong sun flare, and a birdhouse sits in the middle of the frame competing with the bark. The upward view and glare leave the ridges hard to read.
Sharp close frame of grey, lichen-flecked bark with long narrow ridges and scaly plates; no trunk edge or scale object, so it shows texture only.

A slender, smooth, lichen-spotted trunk seen from a distance in a busy autumn forest; the bark is small in the frame and the colourful background competes with it. Young smooth bark is not the usual mature look.
Old trunk with shaggy bark in long, curling, loose vertical plates, with a hand at the left edge for scale; the pattern reads clearly.
Many clusters of red samaras on bare twigs seen from below against a pine; each samara is small in the frame, so kind and shape take a search, and the view from below is an unusual angle.
Close view of paired samaras hanging on long red stalks against a soft green background; full shape but still pinkish and not dry, so unripe.
Lower trunk with its edges and base in a lawn; grey bark with shallow vertical ridges and flaky strips is readable.
Crowded green and pink samaras on stalks against a dark background; full shape but unripe, overlapping and cut by the frame, with strong side light and deep shade changing the colour.
Close frame of old bark with scaly plates and deep furrows, no trunk edge or scale object, so too close; warm low sun tints the colour.
A cluster of red samaras hanging on long stalks from a twig against a soft background; not yet dry so unripe, and warm low sun changes the colour.
Pale samaras among young leaves on a branch seen from below against the sky; samaras are small and mixed with leaves, so a search is needed, and backlight washes the colour.
Close frame of grey-brown bark with long scaly ridges and shallow furrows; no trunk edge or scale object, so too close.
Paired samaras hanging on long red stalks from a twig against soft green foliage; full shape but still pink and fresh, so unripe.
Tiny newly formed red samaras on upright green stalks against a soft background; the wings have not reached full shape, so kind and shape take close study.
One whole hanging sugar maple leaf against a dark background; lobes and sparse teeth are clear. Flash lighting with a black background shifts the leaf colour, so light is listed.
Clusters of red, still-developing red maple samaras hanging from a twig in spring. The samaras have not reached full shape, so young is listed.

Several green sugar maple leaves on a branch with a busy park background; the front-left leaf shows its full outline. Other leaves and the background compete, so alone is false; small brown spots do not change the outline.
Long-stalked clusters of red maple samaras hanging from pale branches, shot with flash against a black background. The flash changes the colour, so light is listed.
A whole, flat, green sugar maple leaf on a plain black background; outline, lobe tips and margin are all clear.
Drooping long-stalked red maple flowers on a twig in early spring, with no formed samaras, leaves or bark. Flowers take the place of the feature.

A pile of fallen orange-red sugar maple leaves; the central leaf is overlapped by others, so its outline takes study and whole is false. Autumn colour gives growth_stage autumn and usual_look false; the dark spots do not change the outline.
Red red maple samaras hanging from a twig against blue sky, nearly full shape but not ripe. The view is from below against the sky, so angle is listed.
One whole green sugar maple leaf laid on bark mulch; outline and margin are clear. Shade gives the leaf a bluish cast, so light is listed.
A sugar maple crown in orange autumn colour where the leaves blend into a mass. No single leaf margin can be read.
A mature trunk with both edges in frame, showing grey plates and long strips that curl away at the edges. The street and building behind are secondary.
One whole green five-lobed leaf on a white background, upper side, with clear lobes, sinuses, and margin. No twig and no scale object.
A whole sapling in a garden bed, with hostas and arborvitae around it. The leaves blend into a mass, and no single leaf's lobes or margin can be read.
The underside of a hanging lobed leaf, with its outline and margin readable. A second leaf and the busy foliage behind it compete, so alone is false.
A mature trunk with both edges in frame, showing furrowed, plated bark. Patches of lichen hide part of the bark colour.
An old forked trunk, shot from a distance with the camera tilted up into the autumn crown. Dappled sun and shade make the bark texture and pattern hard to read.
A close crop of plated, flaking bark with no trunk edge and no scale object. A strong reddish-orange cast changes the bark colour.
A whole sapling in a garden under a spruce, with a fence behind it. The leaves blend into a mass, and the margin of no leaf can be read.
A view up into an orange autumn crown against the sky. The backlit leaves blend into a mass, and no single leaf can be read.
Fallen autumn leaves in a pile on the ground, with a yellow-orange leaf in the centre. The subject is dead, fallen leaf litter, with spotting and other leaves crowding it.
Twig with a hanging cluster of green-seeded samaras and leaves, flash-lit on black. Leaves compete with the fruit, the fruit is full shape but not ripe, and flash changes the colour.
Lichen-covered trunk at a fork, shot slightly upward against a bright sky. The plate pattern is partly hidden by lichen, so it takes study.
Straight trunk with clear long furrows and curling plates, trunk edges in frame.
Camera looks up the trunk into the crown, so the bark recedes and the pattern is hard to read.
A ripe, brown paired samara on a plain background with a 1 cm scale bar; detached, so hang is not shown.
Trunk with dark, shaggy vertical plates and edges in frame; pattern reads well.
Close bark texture with lichen and vertical plates; no trunk edge or scale object.
Close view of grey bark with long curling vertical plates; no trunk edge or scale object.
Trunk with dark plated ridges and trunk edges in frame; pattern is readable.
An old, gnarled, mossy trunk base seen from a distance in dappled sun. The bark is small in the frame, and moss and sun patches hide the pattern.

A single fallen half-samara lying on snow and germinating, with a root emerging. The germinating seed is not the typical fruit form (atypical), and the fruit is past seed fall, so it is not the usual look.
A cluster of paired samaras hangs on long stalks against a soft background, with a leaf at the right. The seeds are green but full size, so the fruit is unripe and not the usual look.
Lobed leaves seen from below against the sky. The central leaf is whole, but crowded leaves compete with it; the view from below adds angle and the backlight adds light.
A whorl of lobed leaves at a shoot tip, seen from above, with the stalks joining the twig. A dense background of other leaves competes with them, so alone is false.
One lobed leaf with insect holes and galls along a lobe (damaged), and the frame edge cuts off its base. Other leaves around it compete with it.
A dense cluster of samaras with green seeds hangs from a twig, with leaves beside it, photographed against black. The crowded fruits make shape need study, and the flash lighting changes the colour.

A leafy branch with a few small green acorns, seen from below against the sky. The leaves overlap, so the outline and margin of one leaf need study; the angle from below and the backlight add angle and light.
A branch spray with many small, wet, lobed leaves over leaf litter. The leaves are crowded and each is small in the frame, so one leaf outline needs a search.
Ripe brown paired samaras hang from stalks in front of bare branches. Warm, low, backlit sun changes their colour (light).
The pale underside of one lobed leaf against a dark background. The frame edges cut off its base and a lobe tip, and the flash-like light with deep shadow changes the colour.
The camera looks up the trunk into the crown, against a bright sky. The ridges are foreshortened and backlit, so this is bark_up_or_dark.
Green acorns with warty caps sit on the twig among lobed leaves. The fruit is unripe, and the large leaves compete with it in the frame.
A mature trunk with both edges in frame shows light grey, scaly, plated bark that is easy to read.
A wide trunk with its edges visible shows the grey blocky plates clearly, in even light.
One green acorn sits behind a large lobed leaf, which hides its lower part and fills most of the frame. Taken at a low side angle, so the outline and the way the acorn sits take study.
A hanging branch with many overlapping lobed leaves. They are crowded and small in the frame, and patchy bright sun bleaches some of them, so finding the outline of one leaf takes a search.
A trunk in a forest, with its edges visible, shows small grey blocky plates clearly. The background is busy but stays behind the trunk.
A large trunk with scaly ridged bark. Strong dappled sun and shadow break up the plate pattern and change the colour.
A trunk with both edges in frame shows light grey, scaly, plated bark clearly.
A studio shot of two ripe brown acorns on a plain blue background, one with its warty cap, with a 1 cm scale bar. Removed from the tree, so the way the acorn hangs does not show.
Dead brown oak leaves in the litter, crowded together, with hard low-sun shadows. The subject is a dead leaf, so it is a reject.
A cluster of green acorns with warty cups on the twig among lobed leaves. The acorns are full shape but unripe.
A cluster of green acorns with warty cups on the twig, framed by lobed leaves. The acorns are full shape but unripe; one is partly hidden behind the others.
A scene of a small tree in red autumn colour among conifers. The main subject is the whole crown, so no single leaf, bark, or fruit can be read.
A branch of red autumn leaves against a soft conifer background. The leaves are small in the frame, overlap, and the photo is slightly soft, so the outline and margin need close study.
A top-down view of a green whorl of lobed leaves on a sapling over leaf litter. The central leaves show their bristle-tipped lobes in full; the stalk joins are small at the centre.
Several acorns with warty cups, green to pink and not yet brown, against a dark flash-lit background. The flash shifts the colour, and the twig attachment is only partly visible.
One green lobed leaf with bristle tips, seen from below against the sky. Backlight lights the leaf through, which changes its colour.
One green acorn in a warty cup on its twig among leaves. It is full shape but unripe.
A cluster of yellow-orange lobed leaves in strong sun against darker green foliage. The bright warm light changes the colour, and the other leaves around the cluster compete with it.
Trunk shot looking straight up into the green crown; the lower bark shows clear striped ridges, but the camera looks up into the crown, which is a reject. The upward view is an unusual angle.

A cluster of green lobed leaves at a shoot tip over leaf litter; the centre leaves show outline and bristle-tipped lobes clearly. Many leaves crowd the frame, so alone is false, and dappled sun puts patchy light on them.

Branch of green lobed leaves against a soft background; the central leaves show full outlines and pointed lobe tips, and stalks join the twig. Leaves overlap and several are tilted, so alone is false and angle applies.

Newly expanding pale spring leaves with small catkins, hanging and backlit against a soft woodland background. The leaves are young, droop and overlap, so the outline needs study; backlight changes the colour.
A spray of green lobed leaves held flat against a trunk, with stalks meeting at the twig tip; outlines and margins read clearly against the bark background.
Branch of many green lobed leaves; the central leaves show full outlines and bristle-tipped lobes. Leaves crowd and overlap and several are tilted, so alone is false and angle applies.
Trunk photographed from the base looking up into the crown; the bark is dark and its striped ridges are only traceable with study. The upward view and the dark exposure make it a reject.
Young yellow-green spring leaves with hanging catkins, strongly backlit. The leaves are not yet full shape, overlap and tilt, so outline and edge need close study; catkins compete with the leaves.
A section of crown in red autumn colour; the small leaves blend into a mass of branches and foliage, so no single leaf reads. Autumn colour sets growth stage autumn.
Base of a large trunk in full width, with clear grey interlacing ridges and furrows. A small dark tag on the trunk is not readable, so it is not a name label.
Close frame of ridged and furrowed bark with lichen and no trunk edge, so too_close. Warm low sun tints the bark orange, which shifts the colour.
Newly unfolding leaves and stipules on a shoot tip against the sky in spring. The leaves are young and half folded, seen from the side, so the outline takes study.
One ripe acorn with its scaly cap hangs from a twig against a soft background. Every feature is easy to read.
Five ripe, capped acorns lie on a plain white surface. The shape and cap read well; how they hang is not shown.
Specimen photo on a blue background with a 1 cm scale bar: one capped acorn, one nut with a cut base, and one nut seen from the top. The top and base views are unusual angles.
A crowded branch of tulip-shaped leaves with many open flowers among them. The flowers and overlapping foliage compete with any one leaf, but the leaf outline still reads.
Dense, overlapping leaves around a flower bud, so no single outline stands clear and leaves are cut by others. Dappled shade and bright gaps darken parts of the leaves.
Green, full-size acorns with caps sit on twigs among leaves and branches. They are unripe, and the busy twigs and leaves compete with them.
A mature trunk filling the frame with both edges visible, showing grey shallow ridges and furrows in even light. Everything reads clearly.
Four acorn views on a black background, including a top view of a cap and a base view of a nut, which are unusual angles. Flash-like lighting makes the nuts look pale grey.
View up into a crown of yellowing autumn leaves against an overcast sky; the leaves blend into a mass and no single outline reads. Upward angle and backlight from the sky.
A crown section with many leaves and a few orange flowers; the leaves blend into a mass and no single leaf stands out. Mixed shade and bright sky gaps.
A trunk with both edges in frame showing fine interlacing furrows, with lichen patches over parts; a street scene behind is soft and does not compete.
One whole green tuliptree leaf on a dark plain background; the four-lobed outline with the notched tip and the entire margin read clearly. A few small spots do not change the outline.

One whole green leaf held over a soft background of fallen yellow leaves; the notched tip, lobes, and entire margin are clear. The fallen leaves suggest autumn but the leaf itself is green and mature.
A crowded cluster of leaves around a flower bud; the lobed outlines overlap and are cut by other leaves, so shape and margin need a search. Arrangement is partly visible at the shoot.
A flowering twig whose main subject is two open tuliptree flowers, with partial leaves around them cut by the frame; deep shade on several leaves.
A crown edge seen from below against blue sky in warm low sun; the leaves are small and blend into a mass, so no leaf outline or margin can be read.
A frame-filling close view of interlacing vertical ridges and furrows; the pattern reads clearly but there is no trunk edge or scale object, so it is too close.
A low sprout among other ground plants with deeply and irregularly lobed leaves unlike the typical four-lobed mature leaf; this is a sucker or sprout form, and other plants crowd the frame.
Straight trunk with both edges in frame; narrow interlacing furrows and flat ridges read clearly against a dark background.
Close frame of furrowed bark with no trunk edge or scale, so too_close; heavy yellow-green lichen hides the bark colour.
The camera looks up the trunk into the crown, so the bark pattern foreshortens and is only readable near the base; reject bark_up_or_dark.
Trunk with both edges and shallow interlacing furrows; dappled sun with pale patches alters the bark colour.
Two children stand in front of a large trunk and cover the lower bark, competing as subjects; the furrow pattern above them is readable only with study.
Trunk with both edges in frame shows clear interlacing furrows and pale inner fissures; background is soft.
Wide trunk with edges against sky; long interlacing ridges with pale furrow bottoms read clearly.
Close frame of thick, criss-crossing ridges with no trunk edge or scale object, so too_close.
Large trunk seen from a distance in a forest, in deep shade with saplings and twigs in front; the furrow pattern is readable only with study.
Several trunks in a leafless winter stand, seen from a distance; branch shadows fall across the bark, and the fine furrows need close study.
One upright brown cone of samaras on its twig against a soft green background; outer samaras slightly spread. Individual samara wings are visible only on close study.
Top view of an opened cone: the outer samaras spread in a star around the bare central axis, against snow. The top view hides the cone outline, so kind and shape take study (angle).
A green, full-shape but unripe cone of samaras upright on its twig among leaves. Unripe, so the samaras are not separable and the kind takes study.
A single dry cone of samaras on a black flash-lit background; only a stub of stalk shows, so the hang takes study. Flash light changes the colour.
Two partly opened cones upright on a twig, small in the frame against busy autumn foliage, so kind and shape need a search.
Frost-covered cones upright on bare twigs against blue; the central cone is intact, others have shed samaras and compete in the frame.
A fallen, bleached cone breaking apart on the ground among shed samaras and litter of the same colour; the disintegrating form is atypical and the litter competes with it.
A brown, spreading cone of samaras in front of soft autumn foliage and leaves; its attachment to the twig is not clearly shown.
One dry cone of samaras upright on a bare twig against a soft blue sky and branches.
A view up into a crown full of small fruits and a few autumn leaves against the sky; no single part is the subject, so the part is other.
Open tulip-shaped cone of samaras on its stalk, against snow, after most seeds have fallen. Clear and alone; it is the winter after-seed-fall form, so not the usual look.

View from below into bare winter branches with small opened samara cones scattered against the sky. The fruits are tiny in the frame and the twigs compete, so kind and shape need a search; upward angle.
Shoot tip with several crowded leaves, many red-brown new leaves that are not yet full form, backlit against bright sky. Top leaf outline readable; the small teeth need a search.
Small sharp photo of one mature sycamore leaf on its twig, lobes and coarse teeth clear. Backlit so the leaf looks translucent yellow-green.
Whole sapling and shrubby growth; the leaves blend into a mass. No single leaf margin can be read.
Upper side of one green leaf with dark spotting, overlapped by neighbouring leaves at the edges. The spots do not change the outline; nearby leaves compete.
Two overlapping leaf undersides held by a hand in front of the mottled trunk. The front leaf overlaps the rear one and fingers touch the edge, so not whole; the shallow teeth need a closer look.
One mature leaf, upper side, against soft lawn, with lobes, coarse teeth and palmate veins all clear.
Sunlit shoot with several green leaves on an alternate stem against a dark background. Top leaves read clearly but several leaves crowd the frame.
Leaf seen from below, backlit, with overlapping leaves behind it and a small fruit ball at the top left. The backlight changes the colour and the view from below adds angle.

One whole lobed leaf with toothed margin on a black night background; flash lighting and brown spots on neighbouring leaves, the spots do not change the outline. Petiole runs up to the twig but the join is small and dark.
Old multi-stemmed trunk base seen from a distance among dense green vegetation; the white and brown mottled patches are readable but the surface texture needs close study.
One whole palmately lobed leaf with toothed margin against a soft gravel background; the petiole join to the twig is not clearly in frame.
View up into a bare winter crown with branches against the sky; no leaf, bark area, or fruit is the main subject.

A shoot of several overlapping leaves laid on boards, showing alternate attachment along the twig; leaves are crowded and the lowest are cut by the frame, but the upper leaves show whole outlines and toothed margins.
Trunk base at a street curb with parked cars competing in the frame; the pale mottled patches at the base read clearly but the texture is small from this distance, and part of the trunk is in shade.
Trunk with peeling plates exposing pale inner bark, plus smooth white branches; warm low light gives the scan a yellowish cast.
A central whole lobed leaf with toothed margin and its petiole joining the twig, but surrounded by overlapping leaves that crowd the frame; small holes do not change the outline.
The camera looks up the white mottled upper trunk into the crown against blue sky, with twigs crossing in front, so it is a bark_up_or_dark reject.
Close frame of the camouflage bark with green, white and reddish peeling patches; texture only, with no trunk edge or scale object.
Green, immature seed ball on its stalk against a leaf; kind and outline read clearly. Young fruit, not yet ripe, so not the usual look.
Base of an old trunk with dark scaly bark and some pale patches on the root flare; shot from a distance with lawn, curb and a car competing, so texture and pattern need close study.
View up into a leafless crown of white branches against the sky; main subject is the crown, not a bark area, so part is other.
Fallen seed ball lying on a log, with the achenes worn off to a pitted core and a broken top; atypical broken ball seen from above.
Whole trunk with flaking brown plates over pale inner bark, trunk edges visible; peeling pattern reads clearly.
Many seed balls hanging on bare branches against the sky, viewed from below; each ball is small in the frame, so kind and shape need a search.

Pale white upper trunk and limbs with brown bark lower down, shot upward among leaves; the white mottled pattern is clear but the texture is distant, and the view looks up into the crown along the trunk.
Single ripe brown seed ball hanging on its stalk, sharp against a soft background; warm low sun tints the colour.
Close view of camouflage-patch bark in grey, cream and green with a burl; texture only, no trunk edge or scale, so too close.
Smooth mottled grey-green and cream trunk with a branch scar, trunk edges visible; surrounding leaves and yellow flowers compete in the foreground.

A single seed ball hangs from its stalk against a soft winter background, but it is breaking apart into fluffy achenes, so the typical tight ball form is lost (atypical) and the fruit kind takes close study.
Many ripe brown seed balls hang on long stalks from bare twigs against a plain blue sky. The view is from below (angle).

Upper side of a green lobed leaf held by a hand; the frame cuts off the top and right lobes (whole false) and other leaves crowd behind it (alone false). Some discoloured spots do not change the outline.
A small young seed ball with styles still showing hangs on its stalk below a twig with an unfolding leaf, against a soft green background; the fruit has not reached full form (young).
A green, full-size seed ball hangs from its stalk against a soft background of autumn leaves; it is not yet ripe.
A seed ball broken open on a log, its fluffy achenes spread out around the core (atypical), seen from the top (angle); the ball kind and outline take close study.
Five ripe brown seed balls hang singly on long stalks from a bare twig against a plain blue sky, seen from below (angle).
A large yellow-green seed ball hangs on its stalk from a pale twig, seen from below against the sky (angle); it is not yet brown and ripe, and other balls show softly behind.
A single greenish seed ball hangs on a long stalk from a bare budded twig against a soft grey background; its green colour marks it as not fully ripe.
A scene of a path lined with planetrees and their green crowns; no single leaf, bark area, or fruit is the subject, so the part is other.
A spray of overlapping green leaves in front of a mottled trunk; the leaves crowd each other and the bark competes, so the outline needs study. Dim, shaded film light.
One large lobed leaf held by a hand against the peeling trunk; the frame edge cuts the right lobe, and the trunk and other leaves compete.
A view into the crown where many leaves blend into a mass; no single leaf reads.
Trunk with flaking plates and cream and grey-green patches; the trunk edges show.
Trunk with brown flaking plates over pale cream patches and some lichen, trunk edges visible against a plain background.
A single lobed leaf held in a hand, underside showing; small spots do not change the outline.
A fallen brown dead leaf on grass among other dead leaves.
A branch seen from below with crowded, backlit leaves and one small seed ball; no single leaf stands out, so outline and edge need study.
A street scene lined with planetrees, with cyclists; no single leaf, bark, or fruit is the subject.
One lobed toothed leaf, shown whole and sharp against a dark soft background, with other leaves below.
View from below into the crown against blue sky: leafy branches with several small green seed balls; no single part is the main subject. Upward angle and backlight on the leaves.
Trunk section with its right edge and fallen autumn leaves behind; flaking patches are partly masked by heavy lichen, so the pattern takes close study.
Close view of peeling bark plates with no trunk edge or scale. Warm low sun and hard shadows shift the colour.
Camera looks up a forked trunk into a bare winter crown; the bark is dark and against bright sky, so the patchwork is hard to read.
Whole trunk width with both edges, showing pale mottled bark with small flaking plates.
Crowded, overlapping backlit leaves beside a peeling trunk; no single leaf outline stands alone and the backlight washes out the edges.
Trunk with both edges, smooth bark with a clear camouflage patchwork of white, green-grey and tan.
Close view of rough, scaly old bark with no trunk edge; dappled light and deep shade on the right obscure the plate pattern and colour.
Close view of colourful exfoliating patches with no trunk edge or scale object.
Narrow trunk with both edges against a building, showing clear flaking brown, cream and green patches; green leaves at the edge.
A dense mass of green foliage with a few small fruit balls; no single leaf stands out, so the leaves blend into a mass and outline and margin need a search.
A single green spiky seed ball on its stalk rests in a hand, with leaves behind; full shape but unripe. Held in hand, so the hang reads only with study; only one ball shows.
A breaking-up brown seed ball lies on paving with loose hairy seeds around it, seen from above; the broken ball is atypical and its outline is ragged.
A small green seed ball hangs in an autumn scene of brown leaves and a trunk in warm low sun; the ball is small in the frame and competes with the leaves, and the light shifts the colour.
A single green spiky seed ball hangs from its stalk among leaves; full shape but unripe.
A single yellow-green spiky seed ball hangs on a long stalk against a soft background; the twig attachment is out of frame, and the ball is not yet ripe.
Two ripe brown seed balls hang one below the other on one stalk against a soft winter sky; the attachment to the twig is only partly shown.
Several ripe brown seed balls hang from bare twigs, seen from below against a bright sky that darkens them; several balls and twigs share the frame.
A single dark brown seed ball hangs from its twig among green leaves, seen from below with backlight that darkens it.
Two yellow-green seed balls hang on one stalk under a leaf, with a third ball behind; full shape but not yet ripe.

A single brown, bristly seed ball is held in a hand by its short stalk, against a soft background of fallen leaves; the kind and round outline read clearly. It is held in the hand, so how it hangs on the twig does not show, and only one ball is present, so two_heads is no.

One whole three-lobed leaf with a toothed edge, still on the twig, in red, orange and green autumn colour in front of hemlock and leaf litter. Autumn colour makes it not the usual look, and its stalk join is hidden.

Many overlapping autumn leaves hang from twigs, backlit by strong sun. The leaves hang at a slant and overlap, so you have to study the outline and edge closely to read them, and the backlight changes their colour.

A carpet of fallen red and brown leaves on the ground, mixed with other species, with some pale undersides showing. The subject is dead, fallen leaf litter, and the crowded leaves mean you have to search to find each outline.
A branch of three-lobed, toothed leaves in red and green autumn colour, with several whole outlines. The leaves crowd each other, and the red stalks join the twig only in part of the frame.
One red three-lobed leaf lies fallen on brown leaf litter beside a mushroom. It is a dead, fallen leaf, and its small teeth need close study at this size.
A crowded spray of green, toothed, three- to five-lobed leaves on red stalks, with a few curled leaves showing pale undersides. The overlap hides most single outlines, so shape needs a search.
A scene of a sapling with red and orange autumn leaves among green trees, grass and asters. The small leaves blend into a mass and the leaf edge cannot be seen.
A cluster of three-lobed, toothed leaves in green, yellow, orange and red, with red stalks that join the twig in view, set against softer red foliage. Autumn colour makes it not the usual look.
One whole green three-lobed leaf with a toothed edge hangs from a red stalk against a soft background. The point where the stalk joins the twig is at the top edge and hard to read.
A close view of one red and green autumn leaf with a sharp toothed edge and clear veins, surrounded by other leaves. The left lobe reaches the frame edge, so the whole outline is in doubt.

A crowded mass of yellow autumn leaves fills the foreground, with a whole red tree behind; the leaves overlap and blend, so no single outline is readable and the margin teeth do not show. Autumn colour sets growth_stage autumn and usual_look false.
The whole lower trunk is shown from a distance, and green moss covers much of the bark, so the strips and their colour need close study. Nothing else competes with the trunk.
A three-stemmed trunk with furrowed, scaly bark; sun glare from behind the middle stem puts the bark in shade, so the ridge pattern and colour need a closer look. Backlight is the cause listed.
A close-up of grey bark with scaly plates and dark vertical furrows; it shows only texture, with no trunk edge or scale object. The far left and right edges are soft, but the centre is sharp.
A straight grey trunk with long, narrow, shaggy vertical ridges, with both trunk edges in frame against a soft forest background. Nothing makes it harder.

A trunk with both edges in frame: mostly smooth light-grey bark that is starting to break into brown, flaking vertical strips. It is a transitional younger bark, not the full mature form, so usual_look is false.
The camera looks up the trunk into the crown, with a birdhouse that competes with the bark and a strong sun flare that washes out the right side. The scaly texture shows only on the lower trunk.
A sharp close-up of grey bark with vertical ridges, scaly plates, and lichen. It shows texture only, with no trunk edge or scale object, so too_close is true.
A slender, dark, fairly smooth trunk with lichen spots, shot from a distance in a busy autumn forest with other trunks nearby. The bark is small in the frame, and the background competes with it.
A large trunk with shaggy bark in long vertical plates that peel at the edges. A hand at the left gives scale and covers no key area. The small file is sharp.

Many clusters of red samaras hanging on leafless twigs, seen from below against a pine and blue sky. The clusters are small and crowded in the frame, so the samara outline and wings need close study, and the upward view is an unusual angle.
Close view of pink-red paired samaras hanging on long red stalks from a twig, with soft young foliage behind. Kind, outline, wings, and hang are all easy to read.

Lower trunk of a forked tree on a lawn, grey bark with shallow vertical ridges and some flaking near the base. The bark is shown from a distance, so the surface texture needs close study, though the ridge pattern reads.

Sunlit cluster of green and pink paired samaras against a dark background; the samaras are full shape but still green, so unripe. The cluster is crowded with overlapping samaras, and only the stalks, not the twig, show how they hang.

Full-frame bark with scaly, flaking plates and narrow vertical ridges, typical of old bark. The frame shows texture only with no trunk edge or scale, and warm low sunlight with deep shadows tints the colour.

Paired samaras hanging on long red stalks from a budded twig, against blue sky and a soft red background of flowering branches. The samaras look full shape but not yet ripe, and warm sunlight shifts their colour toward orange.

Branch with pale tan samara clusters among young green leaves, seen from below against the sky with a house behind. The samaras are small and mixed with leaves and branches, the view is upward, and the bright sky washes out their colour.
Full-frame grey-brown bark with scaly, flaking plates and shallow vertical furrows, typical of old bark. The frame shows texture only, with no trunk edge, branch, or scale object.
Clusters of pink-red paired samaras hanging on long red stalks from a twig, with a young leaf and soft foliage behind. Kind, outline, wings, and hang are all easy to read.

Very young samaras just after flowering, with small red-tipped wings on upright green stalks against a soft background. They have not reached full shape, so the samara form and wings need close study, and the photo does not show how they sit on the twig.

One whole green lobed leaf hangs on its stalk against a black background, with outline, margin and veins readable. The flash and black background make the leaf look grey-green (light); no twig shows, so arrangement is no.
Clusters of full-size red paired samaras hang on long stalks from a leafless twig, against a soft background of blurred branches and sky. Kind, wing and hang are all easy to read.

Several green lobed leaves on a twig in a park, with the front-left leaf whole and readable. Other leaves and a busy background compete (alone false), and you have to look closely to see where the stalks join the twig. The small brown spots do not change the outline.

Dense clusters of red-orange samaras hang from pale branches against a black, flash-lit background. The samaras overlap and are small in the frame, so a learner has to study them to trace one outline (shape search). The flash shifts their colour (light).
A flat scan of one whole green five-lobed leaf with its stalk, on a black background. Outline, lobe tips, margin and veins are all clear, and no twig shows.

Drooping clusters of long-stalked red flowers, possibly just-set fruit with no wings yet, on a leafless branch against an overcast sky. No samara, leaf or bark can be read, so flowers take the place of the feature.

A fallen yellow-red lobed leaf lies in a pile of leaves of the same colour, so you have to look closely to trace its outline and edge (crowded leaves). It shows autumn colour and fungal spots but is not brown. A shadow across the upper part changes the colour (light).
Three clusters of full-size red paired samaras hang from a twig against a plain blue sky. Their kind, wings and hang are all clear.
One whole green lobed leaf with its stalk lies flat on bark mulch, with outline, lobe tips, margin and veins all readable. The mulch is busy but does not compete, and no twig shows.
An orange-yellow autumn crown seen from below fills the frame, and the leaves blend into a mass. Only a few small leaf outlines can be traced, and no margin can be read.
Trunk at eye level with both edges in frame, showing grey-brown bark in long vertical plates that curl away at the edges. The street and building behind it are secondary.
One whole green leaf, upper side, laid on a plain white background. Lobes, sinuses, and margin are all easy to read. No twig shows, so arrangement is no, and no scale object is in frame.
A whole sapling in a garden bed, so the part is other. Its leaves blend into a mass and no single leaf can be read. The hostas and arborvitae around it compete with it.

The pale underside of one hanging leaf, with lobes, margin, and veins clear. A second leaf overlaps it at lower right in front of busy foliage, so alone is false. The petiole's join to the twig is out of frame.
Lichen-patched grey trunk with both edges in frame, showing vertical ridges and plates over a wide area. A few vines and leaves sit at the edges but do not compete.

A large old multi-stemmed trunk shot from the base, looking up into the spreading limbs and the autumn crown, so this is bark_up_or_dark. The bark is seen from a distance under patchy sun and shadow, so texture and pattern are search, and the forest behind competes.

A close-up of bark texture only: flaky plates and vertical fissures fill the frame, with no trunk edge or scale object, so too_close is true. A warm reddish cast changes the bark colour, so light is a cause and colour is search.
A whole sapling in a shaded garden under a spruce, so the part is other. Its leaves overlap into a mass, and the spruce, fence, and hostas compete with it.

A section of crown in orange and red autumn colour, seen against the sky. The small leaves blend into a mass, so the part is other and no single leaf can be read. usual_look is false because of the autumn colour.

Fallen yellow and orange leaves lying in a pile on the ground. The central yellow leaf's lobes and margin are readable. The subjects are dead, fallen leaves among other brown leaves, so this is dead_leaf, and alone is false. The autumn colour sets usual_look to false.

A twig with leaves and hanging clusters of paired samaras on a black background. The samaras overlap, so one fruit outline takes a search; the leaves compete with the fruit; the seeds are still green (unripe); and the flash against black shifts the colour.
A grey, mossy trunk at a fork against blue sky. The scaly texture is readable lower down, but the plate pattern is subtle at this distance. The view tilts up the trunk.
A trunk with long vertical plates that lift at the edges, set against a building. The texture and the plate pattern are both easy to read.
Taken from the base of a large old tree, looking up into the green crown. Rejected because the camera looks up into the crown, so the bark ridges show only on the foreshortened lower trunk.
One dry, tan double samara with its stalk on a plain studio background, with a 1 cm scale bar. The kind, the shape, and the wings are clear. The fruit is detached, so it does not show how it hangs.
A trunk with long, dark grey plates that curl at the edges, against a park background. The texture and the plate pattern read easily.
A full-frame close-up of mossy grey bark with furrows and loose plates. It has no trunk edge, branch, or scale object, so it is too close.
A full-frame close-up of grey bark in long vertical plates that curl outward. The pattern is clear, but the frame has no trunk edge or scale, so it is too close.
A trunk with scaly plates and furrows in front of a brick building, seen from a slight upward view. The texture and the pattern are readable.
The lower trunk and branches of an old, gnarled tree in grass, taken from a distance. The plates and texture take a search, and strong sun with dappled shade changes how the bark looks.

One detached samara lying on snow, germinating, with a radicle coming out of the seed, on a plain background. It is atypical because it is a single germinating half, not the paired samara on the twig, so it should not test fruit kind. It is fallen fruit, so hang is no, and the germination marks it as spring.

A cluster of paired samaras hangs on long stalks from the twig against a soft background, with part of a leaf at the right. The fruit has its full shape, but the seeds are still green, so it is unripe and not the usual look.
Lobed oak leaves seen from below against a bright sky. The leaves overlap and crowd each other, so alone is false. The view from below is the angle cause, and the backlight changes the leaf colour.

A cluster of whole lobed leaves at the tip of a twig, with the petioles meeting at the twig, in front of a background of more leaves of the same kind. The front leaves are lit and the background falls off to dark, which looks like flash and gives the leaves a grey-blue cast.
A close view of one lobed leaf with several holes and yellow galls near the lobes, so it is damaged. The top frame edge cuts off the leaf base, so whole is false.

A dense cluster of samaras hangs from a twig on a black background, with leaves at the left. The samaras overlap and are small, so shape is search. The seeds are green, so the fruit is unripe, and the flash on the black background changes the colours.

Two green acorns sit at the centre of a leafy branch against the sky. They are small in the frame and the many lobed leaves around them compete, so the fruit features are search and alone is false. The acorns are green, so they are unripe.

A drooping branch of many wet, lobed leaves over a ground of pine needles. Single leaf outlines can still be traced, so it is not a leaf mass, but the leaves are small and crowded, so the key features are search and alone is false.
A cluster of dry brown paired samaras hangs on stalks from a twig, in front of a soft background of bare branches and blue sky. Warm, low sun lights the wings from behind and changes their colour.

One whole lobed leaf shows its pale underside with raised veins, against a dark background, with part of a second leaf at the lower right. The lit leaf against the dark background looks like flash or a sunlit spot in deep shade, which gives the leaf a grey-blue colour.
The camera looks up the trunk into a backlit green crown. Only the lower trunk shows the scaly bark, so texture and pattern are at search, and the view from below and the backlight are causes.

Green acorns with warty caps sit on a twig among lobed leaves. The acorns are small in the frame and the large leaves compete with them. The view from above hides the nut outline, and the acorns are not ripe.
A broad trunk fills the frame and both edges show. The light grey, scaly vertical plates are easy to read.
A sharp, evenly lit trunk shows its edges and its grey, blocky, scaly plates.
A green acorn with a warty cap rests behind a large lobed leaf. The leaf hides the base of the cap and fills most of the frame, and the acorn is not ripe. The stalk is not shown, so hang is no.
A hanging branch holds many deeply lobed green leaves. They are crowded and overlap, so a learner must search to trace one leaf's outline and edge.
A trunk in a forest shows both edges and small, blocky grey plates. The busy woodland background does not compete with the trunk.
A large trunk in front of a brick building shows its scaly ridged bark. Dappled sun and shade change the colour across the bark, so light is a cause.
A light grey trunk with scaly, flaking plates is sharp and evenly lit, and its edges show.
This specimen shot shows two ripe oblong acorns on a plain blue background with a 1 cm scale bar. One acorn has its warty cap. Neither is shown on a twig, so hang is no.

Dead brown oak leaves in leaf litter; the central leaf's lobes and bristle tips are readable but other leaves overlap it and crowd the frame. Warm low sun with deep shadows changes the colour; the subject is a dead leaf, so it is a reject.
Three green acorns with warty caps on a twig, with lobed leaves around them and a soft background. The acorns are full shape but green, so unripe and not the usual look.
A cluster of green acorns with warty caps on the twig, framed by lobed leaves; fingers holding the branch show at the top left. The acorns are full shape but green, so unripe and not the usual look.
A whole crown in red autumn colour among conifers, cut off at the bottom of the frame; individual leaves blend into a mass. The main subject is a crown, so the part is other.

A spray of red autumn leaves on a branch against a dark conifer background; the leaves are small in the frame, slightly soft, and overlap, so the outline and margin need close study. Autumn colour gives growth stage autumn and not the usual look.

A whorl of green lobed leaves at the tip of a young shoot, seen from above, with the stalks meeting at the twig. The bristle tips are small in the frame, so the margin needs a search, and the leaf litter and other shoots make a busy background.
Several acorns with warty caps against a dark background, only the top one clearly attached to the twig. Flash lighting tints the nuts pink, and the nuts are not yet brown, so unripe.

One whole lobed leaf with bristle-tipped lobes, seen from below with its underside and raised midrib facing the camera. The view from below is an unusual angle; a few small spots do not change the outline.
One green acorn with a warty cap on a short stalk from the twig, among leaves. It is full shape but green, so unripe and not the usual look.
A cluster of yellow-orange lobed leaves at a shoot tip against busy green foliage. Harsh direct sun and strong saturation change the colour; the turning colour reads as autumn, so not the usual look.

Trunk shot from the base looking straight up into the green crown; the ridged 'ski-track' bark is readable on the lower trunk. The camera looks up into the crown, so it is a bark_up_or_dark reject, and the view from below is an angle cause.

Top view of a low cluster of green lobed leaves over leaf litter; the central leaf outline is whole and readable. Neighbouring leaves crowd it (alone false), and the bristle-tipped margin is small in the frame (search).

Several dark green lobed leaves hang from a twig against a soft garden background; a couple of leaves show a whole outline. The leaves overlap and crowd each other (alone false), and the bristle tips are small (margin search).

A spring shoot of soft, pale, backlit new leaves with small catkins at the twig; the lobed outline with bristle tips reads well against a blurred background. The leaves are young (not yet full form) and the backlight turns them yellow-green; the catkins do not replace the leaves.

A short shoot of five shallow-lobed leaves appears to sprout straight from the mossy trunk, i.e. an epicormic/sucker shoot, so it is a sucker_leaf reject. The leaves are sharp and whole, but their shallow lobes are not the typical mature red oak form.
A branch of green, deeply lobed, bristle-tipped leaves, with the twig and leaf stalks visible at the top. Many overlapping leaves crowd the frame, so alone is false.

View from the trunk base up into a large leafy crown against a bright sky; the striped ridges show faintly on a dark, shaded trunk. The camera looks up into the crown (bark_up_or_dark reject); the low angle and backlight darken the bark, and the crown competes for attention.

Spring twigs with pale, backlit young leaves and many hanging catkins; the lobed outlines show but overlap one another and the catkins. The leaves are young, the backlight turns them yellow, and the crowding means no single leaf outline is clean (whole false, shape and margin at search).

A section of crown in red autumn colour; the small leaves blend into a mass among the branches (leaf_mass). Lobe shapes show only with close study and the margin cannot be made out at this size (feature_unclear); autumn colour makes usual_look false.

The lower trunk of a large tree with both edges in frame, showing grey interlacing ridges and furrows over a flared base. A small dark tag is on the trunk at the left, but no text is readable at this size, so it is not a name_label reject.

Close-up of furrowed, ridged bark with lichen. The frame shows texture only, with no trunk edge or scale, so too_close is true. Warm low sun tints the bark golden, so colour is at search and light is listed.
New spring shoot with two young, folded leaves and large stipules, shot from below against the sky. The leaves have not reached full shape and are curled and tilted, so the outline takes close study.
One ripe brown acorn with its scaly cap, hanging from its stalk against a soft background. Sharp and clear.
Five ripe, detached acorns with caps on a plain white cloth. They are off the twig, so hang is no.
Studio seed photo on a blue background with a 1 cm scale bar. It shows one capped acorn from the side plus two capless nut views. Detached, so hang is no.

Flowering branch with many crowded leaves and several tulip flowers, so alone is false. Several leaves show the full four-lobed outline, but they are small in the frame, so the margin takes study. The flowers do not hide the leaves.
Dense green foliage around a green developing cone. The leaves overlap and are tilted, so no outline shows complete: whole and alone are false, shape is at search, and angle is listed.
Studio photo on black: a capped acorn, a capless nut, a cap top view and a nut base view. Flash on the black background washes the acorns to a pale grey-tan, so light is listed.
Three green acorns with caps sit on the twig among leaves, against soft grass. The acorns are full shape but not ripe, so growth_stage is unripe and usual_look is false.
Full trunk width with both edges in frame. It shows grey bark with long, shallow, flat-topped ridges, sharp and evenly lit.

View up into a crown of yellowing autumn leaves against a white sky. The leaves blend into a mass, with only a few outlines traceable; the upward view and backlight are causes, and the autumn colour makes it not the usual look.

Part of a flowering crown with many leaves and several orange flowers. The leaves crowd into a mass, so single outlines are found only with a search; the flowers show the season but do not replace the leaves.

A mature trunk with both edges in frame, fine interlacing furrows, and lichen patches. The furrow pattern is fine at this size and partly hidden by lichen, so it needs close study; a sharp street scene behind the trunk competes with it.
One whole, flat, green tulip-shaped leaf with the petiole, against dark bark. A few small spots do not change the outline.
One whole green leaf with the petiole, against a soft background of fallen yellow leaves. The fallen leaves mark autumn, but the leaf itself is green and mature.
A leafy shoot with a flower bud at the centre and several full tulip-shaped leaves. The leaves overlap and crowd the frame, and the stalk joins at the shoot are seen only with a search.
The main subject is a twig with two open flowers and a flower bud, with shaded leaves around them. The flowers take the place of a leaf or fruit as the subject, so the part is other.
The edge of a crown against a blue sky, seen from below. The leaves are small and blend into a mass; warm low sun and backlight change the colour.
A sharp close-up of interlacing, furrowed grey-brown bark that fills the frame. No trunk edge, branch, or scale object shows, so it is texture only.

Low sprout shoots among ground cover, with irregular, deeply multi-lobed leaves that are not the typical four-lobed tulip form. These look like sucker or sprout leaves, which the mature-tree description does not name, so the photo is a reject. Other plants crowd the frame.
A straight trunk with both edges in frame and narrow interlacing grey ridges with pale furrows. Sun is strong from one side but the colour still reads true.

Close bark texture filling the frame with deep vertical interlacing furrows; no trunk edge, branch, or scale object, so too_close. Heavy yellow-green lichen covers much of the surface, so the bark colour needs close study.
The camera looks up the trunk into the green crown, so bark_up_or_dark; the crown competes with the trunk. The upward angle foreshortens the ridges and dappled sun and shade patch the bark.
A trunk with both edges in frame against a dark soft background, showing shallow furrows with pale whitish patches between them. Small file but sharp.

A very large trunk with two children standing in front of it, covering the lower half; the children compete with the bark. The furrowed bark is seen from a distance in the upper half, so texture and pattern need a search.
A trunk with both edges in frame showing interlacing ridges with pale furrow bottoms and a healed branch scar in the middle. The road and fence behind are soft and do not compete.
A tall trunk against sky with both edges in frame, showing the typical interlacing ridges with whitish furrows. Evenly lit and sharp.

Close bark texture filling the frame with no trunk edge or scale object, so too_close. The ridges run diagonally across the frame, as if the view is tilted, which makes the usual vertical interlacing harder to read.

A large old trunk in a forest seen from a distance, with sapling stems and branches crossing in front. The trunk is in deep shade and the image is dark, so the furrows need a search, but they can still be traced in the upper trunk.

Several leafless trunks in winter, one with a hairy vine, so no one trunk stands alone. The fine furrows are seen from a distance and branch shadows fall across the bark, with one trunk in full shadow.
One dry, brown, ripe cone of samaras sits upright on its twig in side light. The outer samaras are starting to spread, and the background is soft green and yellow foliage.

A top-down view of a cone after seed fall: the outer samaras spread in a star around the bare central axis, against snow. The top view hides the cone's profile and how it sits on the twig, so it gets angle and shape at search.
A green, full-size, unripe cone stands upright on its stalk among out-of-focus leaves. The samaras are tightly packed, so the kind takes close study and no wings show.
A ripe, dry cone of samaras photographed with flash against a black background. Flash is a light cause, and only a stalk stub shows, with no twig, so hang is no.
Two ripe cones sit upright on a bare twig in front of soft autumn foliage. The cones are small in the frame, so their kind, shape, and wings take a search.

Several frosted cones stand on frosty twigs against a deep blue background. The sharp central cone is the subject, but other cones and twigs compete with it, so alone is false. Hoarfrost covers the samara wings, so wing is at search.

A fallen, weathered, bleached-grey cone lies on the ground among leaf litter and clover. Its weathered colour is not the typical look, so it gets atypical, the busy litter competes with it, and nothing shows how it hung.

An opening ripe cone with spreading samaras is in front of soft yellow autumn foliage and part of a leaf. The cone sits in shade against a bright background, which darkens its colour, so it gets light. Its stalk is thin and hard to follow, so hang is at search.
One pale, ripe cone with spreading samaras stands upright on a bare twig. Behind it are a blurred blue sky and bare branches.

The camera looks up into an autumn crown with many small cones and scattered yellow leaves against the sky. The main subject is the crown, not one part, so the part is other, and the view from below adds angle.

One dry, open cone of samaras standing upright on its curved stalk against snow; the persistent outer samaras and their wings read clearly. It is the winter form after the inner samaras have fallen, so it is not the ripe usual look.

Bare winter branches of the crown, seen from below against blue sky, with small persistent samara rosettes scattered through the frame. The main subject is the crown rather than one fruit; the upward view and the sky backlight turn the fruits into small dark silhouettes.

An upright shoot of crowded, overlapping leaves; the top leaf shows a whole lobed, toothed outline. Several leaves have turned red and orange (autumn colour), and backlight from the bright sky changes the leaf colour.

One large leaf with shallow lobes and coarse teeth hangs from a twig against a dark background, with a second leaf and its stalk on the twig above. Strong backlight makes the leaf glow yellow-green and changes its colour.
A sapling or thicket of sycamore foliage with trees behind; the leaves blend into a green mass. Single leaf outlines and teeth can only be found by searching.

A close view of one green leaf with fine dark speckles. A neighbouring leaf, seen from below with white veins, covers its lower left lobe, so the outline is only partly visible and the leaf is not whole; the other leaves crowd the frame.

A hand holds two large overlapping leaves above leaf litter, with a stretch of mottled sycamore bark across the top. The overlap and the fingers at the right lobe hide part of the outline, so the leaf is not whole and its shape and edge take some searching; the hand gives the size.
One whole green leaf against soft grass, showing its shallow lobes, coarse teeth, and palmate veins clearly; part of a second leaf shows at the left edge.

A sunlit shoot with several overlapping green leaves against a dark background; the upper leaves show whole lobed outlines, and the stalks can be seen joining the stem. The leaves crowd each other, and their teeth are small in the frame.

One hanging leaf seen from below in front of a soft street background, with a small young seed ball at the upper left. The frame edges cut off the tips of the right and bottom lobes, and backlight makes the leaf look yellow-green.

One lobed, coarsely toothed leaf, upper side, on a black flash-lit background; outline and teeth read clearly. Flash lighting (light); brown spots on the blade and neighbouring leaves do not change the outline, and the petiole-twig join at the top is tangled (arrangement search).

Lower trunks of an old, hollow multi-stemmed tree seen from a distance; the white-and-brown mottled peeling pattern is visible but the surface texture needs close study (bark from a distance). Weeds in front and busy foliage behind compete (alone false).

One whole lobed, toothed leaf against soft gravel ground; outline and margin clear. The blade is pale and stippled but the outline is intact; the petiole join to the twig is only partly in frame (arrangement search).

Camera looks up into a leafless crown; the mottled bark on the trunk and limbs is small and far, so texture and pattern need close study. View from below (angle) and tangled branches compete (alone false); looking up into the crown is a reject.

A leafy shoot laid on grey decking, upper sides showing; the top leaf shows a whole lobed, toothed outline and the alternate stalk joins are visible. The leaves overlap and crowd the frame (alone false), and the lowest leaves run off the frame edge.

Street scene with a trunk base beside a curb; the mottled grey-and-white lower bark is visible but small and from a distance, so texture and pattern need close study. Cars and the street compete with the trunk (alone false); cars and curb give scale.

Trunk with clear exfoliating patches of cream, grey and brown, trunk edges and crossing limbs in frame, soft background. Warm low light gives the image a faded warm cast (light), though the tree still looks real.

Several overlapping lobed, toothed leaves fill the frame, upper sides showing; the central leaf's outline must be traced among its neighbours (shape search, alone false). A young flower head and new shoots mark spring; small holes do not change the outline.

Looking up the trunk into the crown against blue sky; the white-and-tan mottled peeling bark reads clearly. View from below (angle) and crossing twigs and limbs compete (alone false); the upward view into the crown is a reject.

Close-up of bark showing an olive, white and cream patchwork with reddish peeling flakes; texture and pattern clear. The frame shows texture only, with no trunk edge, branch or scale object (too_close).
A single green seed ball hangs on its stalk in front of a plain leaf; the ball has its full round shape but is not ripe, so growth_stage is unripe and usual_look is false.

The base of an old trunk with dark scaly bark and pale peeling patches at the root flare, shot from a few metres away; the curb, lawn and a car compete with it, and the plate pattern is small in the frame, so pattern is search.
The camera looks up into a bare crown of smooth white limbs against blue sky, so it is a bark_up_or_dark reject; the view from below is an angle cause and the mass of twigs competes with the bark.
An intact brown seed ball lies on a rotting log, with a small broken fragment beside it; the kind and round shape read clearly, but it is on the ground, so hang is no.
A trunk with heavy peeling plates in brown, grey and cream fills the frame from a moderate distance; the peeling pattern and colours read clearly against a forest background.

Many small brown seed balls hang on long stalks from bare twigs, seen from below against blue sky; each ball is small in the frame, so kind and shape are search, and the view from below is an angle cause.
The camera looks up the white, patchy trunk into the leafy crown, so it is a bark_up_or_dark reject; the upward view is an angle cause, and branches, leaves and wires compete with the bark.
A large ripe brown seed ball hangs on its stalk against a soft background of sky and bare branches; its kind, round shape and hanging habit all read clearly.

A close-up of mottled grey, cream and green patchwork bark around a knot; the camouflage pattern reads clearly, but the frame shows texture only, with no trunk edge, branch or scale object, so too_close is true.
A smooth trunk with grey-green and cream peeling patches shows clearly, with both trunk edges in frame; leaves and yellow flower spikes in the foreground overlap it, so alone is false.

A single seed ball hangs from its stalk against a soft sky with bare trees. The ball is breaking apart into fluffy achenes, so it is not the typical round ball. Its outline is ragged, so shape is at search.

Many ripe brown seed balls hang on long stalks from bare branches, seen from below against a blue sky. Each ball is small in the frame, so kind is at search, and the crossing branches and many balls mean the subject is not alone.

Upper side of one lobed, toothed leaf held in a hand, with other leaves crowding the background. The frame cuts off the top lobe tip and the right lobe, so whole is false; brown blotches and a small spot show but do not change the outline. The part is leaf, so the two_heads depth feature does not apply.

A small young seed ball with projecting styles hangs on a green stalk from a twig beside a just-unfolding leaf, on a soft green background. It is the head just past flowering, not yet a full-size ripe ball, so it is young.
A single green seed ball hangs on its stalk, sharp against a soft background of yellow and brown autumn leaves. The ball has full shape but is still green, so it is unripe.

A broken seed ball lies on a log, seen from above, with its core and a ring of hairy achenes splayed out like a flower. The ball form is gone, so kind and shape take close study, and it is atypical with a top view.
Five ripe brown seed balls hang on long single stalks from a bare twig against a plain blue sky. All features read clearly.
A large yellow-green seed ball hangs on a green stalk from a bare twig, with brown balls in the background. The ball has full shape but is still green, so it is unripe.
One olive-green seed ball hangs on a long stalk from a bare budded twig, against a soft grey background. The ball has full shape but is still green, so it is unripe.

A tree-lined path seen under the green crowns of an avenue of trees, so the main subject is a scene, not a leaf, bark, or fruit. The leaves blend into a canopy mass and no single part can be read. The part is not fruit, so the two_heads depth feature does not apply.

Mottled cream and brown patchwork bark on a trunk with both edges in frame. The trunk is slightly soft, so the fine texture needs study (texture search), and a spray of green leaves in the upper left competes with it (alone false).

Large green lobed, toothed leaf held by a hand in front of a mottled trunk. The leaf hangs upside down and tilted (angle). The hand and an overlapping leaf cover the base, and the frame edges clip the side lobe tips (whole false).
Dense canopy of green leaves and twigs. No single leaf stands out, and the outlines blend into a mass, so this is a leaf_mass reject.
Sharp view of a trunk with flaking brown plates over grey-green and cream patches. Both trunk edges show against a soft background. Nothing makes it harder.
Sunlit trunk with a camouflage pattern of brown, olive, and cream patches, and some lichen. The trunk edges show against sky and a soft background. Nothing makes it harder.
Green lobed leaf with coarse teeth, held by a hand. The hand covers the lower left of the blade and another leaf overlaps the right lobe (whole false). The small spots do not change the outline.
Fallen dead brown leaf on grass among other dead leaves. The subject is a dead leaf (dead_leaf reject). The other leaves overlap its lower lobes and compete with it.

One green seed ball hangs on its stalk under backlit foliage, with a parked car behind it. The ball is small in the frame (kind and shape search), it is not ripe yet, the leaves and car compete, and the backlight changes the colours. Only one ball shows (two_heads no).
Street scene with a row of planetrees, a road, and cyclists. No leaf, bark, or fruit is the main subject, so the part is other.
One whole bright green leaf with sharp lobes and coarse teeth on a dark, soft background. The petiole runs toward the twig, but the joint is hard to see (arrangement search).

View from below into leafy branch tips against blue sky, with small green seed balls hanging singly; leaves overlap and are backlit, so lobes and teeth need study (shape and margin search, alone false, angle and light). Leaves stay distinct enough at the top left that it is not a leaf mass.
Trunk with its right edge and a pavement in view; lichen and green algae cover much of the surface, so the patchwork of shed plates is only faintly readable (pattern and colour search).

Close-up of a few peeling bark plates on a smooth trunk, with no trunk edge or scale (too_close). Warm low sun with deep side shadow shifts the colour (light), and the small area shows only a few patches of the repeat (whole false).
Camera looks up a forked trunk into bare winter branches against a bright sky; the trunk is in shade, so the burly and mottled bark is hard to read (bark_up_or_dark, angle, light).
Trunk filling the frame with both edges visible, pale bark broken into small mottled plates with fine dark cracks; potted palms behind do not compete.

Backlit leaves seen from below beside a trunk with peeling bark and overhead wires; leaves overlap and the trunk competes (alone false, shape and margin search), and backlight and the low angle change the look (angle, light).
Smooth trunk with both edges visible and a clear white, grey-green, and tan patchwork of shed plates against soft green woodland.

Close-up of rough, flaking old bark with no trunk edge or scale (too_close); strong raking light leaves the right side in deep shadow, so the plate pattern and colours need study (light, pattern and colour search).
Frame-filling close-up of camouflage bark with yellow, green, and brown patches showing the pattern repeat clearly; no trunk edge or scale, so too_close.
Narrow trunk view with both edges visible and mottled peeling plates against a plain white wall; the small file is sharp.

A close view of crowded, overlapping foliage with a few small green fruit balls. Only the centre leaf stands out, so its lobes and margin need close study (shape and margin at search), the leaves overlap (whole false), and nothing stands alone.

One green, spiky seed ball on its stalk, resting in a hand, with a leaf and foliage behind it. The ball is full size but green (unripe). The large hand and the leaves compete with it, and the hand alters how it hangs (hang at search).

A fallen, ripe seed ball on paving that is breaking apart, with loose hairy achenes around it. It is a broken fruit ball (atypical), but it still reads as a seed ball on a plain background. It is on the ground, so hang is not shown.

An autumn scene in warm, low sun: one greenish seed ball hangs on a long stalk in front of the trunk, among brown leaves. The ball is small in a busy frame (kind at search, alone false), and the low sun warms the colours (light).
One green, spiky seed ball hangs from its stalk among green leaves. It is sharp and central. It is full size but green, so it is unripe and not the usual look.
One green, spiky seed ball hangs from a long stalk against a soft, dark background. It is full size but green, so it is unripe and not the usual look.
Two ripe brown seed balls hang one above the other on one stalk, near a bare twig, against a soft winter sky. The pair on one stalk shows clearly.

Several ripe brown seed balls hang on long single stalks from bare twigs, against a blue sky. The view is from below (angle), and the backlight darkens the balls to near silhouettes (light). No two balls clearly share a stalk.

One dark brown seed ball hangs from a twig among large green leaves, seen from below against a bright canopy. The ball is small in the frame, and the leaves compete with it (kind at search, alone false). The view is from below (angle), and backlight darkens it (light).

Two greenish seed balls hang one below the other on one stalk, with a third ball behind them and a leaf above. The pair on one stalk shows clearly. The balls are full size but still green, so they are unripe and not the usual look.

One brown, bristly, intact seed ball held up by its stalk in a hand, sharp, with soft fallen leaves behind it. The hand hides how the ball hangs, so hang is no, and only one ball shows on the stalk, so two_heads is no. The source name Platanus ×hispanica matches the tree, so the hybrid rule does not apply.
One whole red and green autumn leaf in the centre with the outline and lobe tips readable, against conifer needles that add some clutter. Autumn colour so usual_look is false; it is not a cause.
Backlit cluster of overlapping autumn leaves, with no single leaf outline in full. Outlines and edges can be traced only with study, so shape and margin are search; backlight is the cause.
Top view of a carpet of fallen red and brown leaves that blend into a mass; no single leaf is the subject. Reject as leaf_mass; the top-down view is the angle cause.
Several crowded red and green autumn leaves on a twig; the lobes and toothed margin of the central leaves are readable but the frame edge cuts off other leaves. Crowding makes alone false.
One whole red autumn leaf lying on brown leaf litter, with a mushroom nearby; the red leaf stands out and its outline and margin are clear. Autumn colour so usual_look is false.
Crowded green mature leaves in shade with overlapping outlines, so no single leaf shows in full and shape and margin need study. Shaded light is the cause.
A scene of a small tree or shrub in autumn colour beside a meadow and water; the main subject is the whole plant, not a leaf, so part is other.
Whole green and red autumn leaf with the lobes and teeth readable, but other leaves crowd the background and overlap its sides. Autumn colour so usual_look is false.
One sharp green mature leaf with a red petiole against a soft dark background; outline, lobe tips, toothed margin and veins are all readable.
Large central red and green autumn leaf, sharp and readable, though the left lobe touches the frame edge and other leaves crowd around it. Autumn colour so usual_look is false.

A crowded mass of yellow autumn leaves overlaps in the foreground, with a red tree behind. Outlines and edges can be traced only with study, so shape and margin are search, and the leaves are in autumn colour in strong sun.
Full trunk of a mature tree in a park scene, seen from a distance. The bark is furrowed and partly mossy, so texture and pattern need a search.
A multi-stem trunk with grey furrowed bark, shot from a short distance with bright sky behind. The ridges are visible but the bark pattern needs close study.
A close-up of grey bark with broken ridges and plates. The frame shows texture only, with no trunk edge, branch, or scale, so it is too close.
A whole trunk with narrow vertical furrows and flat ridges, with both trunk edges in the frame. Sharp and well lit.
A trunk with grey-brown peeling plates and lighter patches. A twig and the trunk edges are in the frame.
The camera looks up the trunk into the crown, with the sun in the frame as strong backlight. A birdhouse competes with the bark, and the bark colour is washed out.
A close-up of vertically ridged and flaking bark with lichen. No trunk edge, branch, or scale is in the frame, so it is texture only.
A narrow dark trunk in an autumn forest, with leaf litter and other trees competing. The bark is small in the frame and mostly smooth with lichen patches, so the features need a search.
A trunk with deep, shaggy plates and ridges, with a hand at the left edge for scale. The hand covers only a small part of the bark.
Many red samara clusters across a crown, seen from below against pine and sky. Fruit is small and crowded, so kind, shape and wing take a search; angle is from below.
Sharp close view of hanging paired samaras on red stalks with soft green background. Wings and hang are plain.
Whole lower trunk on a lawn showing vertical ridges and flakes; trunk edges and base are in frame.
Dense overlapping green-and-pink samaras in shade. Full shape but unripe; crowding makes outlines and hang need study.
Tight shot of ridged, flaking bark with no trunk edge, branch or scale. Warm low sun lights it.
Hanging samara pairs on a twig against blue sky and a soft background. Slightly crowded but the wings and pairing are readable.
Samaras hang among leaves and branches in a crown. They are small in the frame and compete with foliage, so kind and shape need a search.
Close, sharp view of ridged and flaking bark. No trunk edge, branch or scale is in the frame.
Sharp hanging paired samaras on red stalks, with a maple leaf and soft background.
Young red-and-green fruits just forming on upright stalks, with small wings and flower remnants. Not yet full shape, so young; blurred background.
One whole upper-side leaf with its stalk against a dark background, outline and lobes readable. Flash or dark surroundings give a grey-green cast, so light.
Clusters of red paired samaras hang from a twig against a soft background. Kind, shape, wing and hang are all readable.
Several overlapping leaves on a branch with a busy park background. The large left leaf is tilted, so angle, and the margin needs a search; brown spots do not change the outline.
Hanging clusters of orange-red samaras on a bare branch, shot at night with flash against black. The flash shifts the colour, so light.
A scanned whole green leaf with its stalk on a plain black background. Outline, lobe tips and margin are sharp.
Red flowers hanging on stalks from a bare twig against a cloudy sky. Flowers only, no leaf, bark or fruit as the main subject.
A pile of fallen autumn leaves in yellow and red, overlapping, with spots. The central leaf is partly cut by the frame edge and overlapped. Autumn colour is not a cause.
Red samaras hanging from twigs against a clear blue sky. Kind, wing and hang all read clearly.
One whole green leaf with its stalk lying on wood mulch. The outline is clear, but the busy mulch competes.
A crown full of orange autumn foliage against blue sky. Leaves blend into a mass, no single leaf is the subject.
Wide trunk with vertical ridges and plates, trunk edges visible, building behind but the trunk dominates.
